protest_portal.name: iFile (HCAD Electronic Filing and Notice System / Owners portal)
protest_portal.requires: Free owners account (owners.hcad.org sign-up) linked to the property. The property's iFile number (printed upper right of the Notice of Appraised Value and on the green protest form) is needed unless the account is already linked; the notice also shows the account number. A lost iFile number can be retrieved with HCAD's free mobile app / features.hcad.org by scanning a Texas driver license whose address matches the account.

counties.filing_notes: Online: iFile through owners.hcad.org is HCAD's preferred method. https://hcad.org/ifile-protest also links a no-account online Notice of Protest form (hcad.seamlessdocs.com/f/NoticeofProtest) under 'No, I don't want to iFile my protest'. Paper: Form 50-132 (Property Appraisal - Notice of Protest; also the protest form enclosed with the notice) can be mailed to Assistance Center, Harris Central Appraisal District, P.O. Box 922004, Houston, TX 77292-2004 (must be postmarked by the deadline; HCAD advises getting the envelope hand-stamped at the post office) or dropped off at 13013 Northwest Freeway during office hours (8 AM-5 PM Mon-Fri; no after-hours drop box). Paper protests do not need an iFile number. No protest fax number or protest email is published (isettle@hcad.org is only for iSettle questions).

informal_hearings.notes: iSettle: online settlement offer for protests filed via iFile on single-family residential accounts (owner must give an email and an opinion of value; evidence upload allowed for 5 calendar days after filing). Informal meetings with an HCAD appraiser are in person or by Webex videoconference (phone can be used for audio once the Webex meeting launches); check-in via owners.hcad.org. Formal ARB hearings can be in person, videoconference, telephone, by agent, or by sworn affidavit; ARB does not accept evidence by email.

counties.notice_timing: HCAD news release dated May 1, 2026 says it had mailed 2026 property value notices to many residential, commercial and industrial owners. Published protest deadline (FAQ and May 6, 2026 release): May 15, or 30 days after the date on the notice, whichever is later; if the notice was not mailed by April 15 the deadline is 30 days after the date printed on the notice. Owners can check notice status / protest deadline on their HCAD property search account page.

HCAD states it provides no technical support for the data. Timeline on page: April preliminary real values, May-August weekly updates, mid-August certified.

protest_portal.name: uFILE Online Protest and Settlement System
protest_portal.requires: No separate login page: search the account first (by owner name, account number or street address), open the account, then select the 'uFile Online Protest' link. Verification needs the account PIN (top-left corner of the Notice of Appraised Value; changes every year) plus an on-screen Security Code. If you have no notice, the uFile screen has a 'Request PIN to be sent by Email' option (requesting a PIN does not file a protest).

counties.filing_notes: DCAD says uFile is its preferred method and 'the only way for property owners to file a protest electronically'; the ARB will NOT accept protests by fax or e-mail. A written protest (an official form is not required, but it must identify the owner and property and show dissatisfaction) can be mailed to the address on the Notice of Appraised Value or to the Dallas County ARB, P.O. Box 560348, Dallas TX 75356-0348, or delivered to 2949 N. Stemmons Freeway (24/7 drop box/lockbox at the west main entrance; doors lock at 5:00 PM on the deadline). Mailed protests need a postmark by the deadline. If uFile upload fails, DCAD tells owners to mail the protest and documents instead.

informal_hearings.notes: A protest must be filed and evidence submitted before DCAD staff will do an Informal Review. After filing via uFile with an opinion of value and documents, appraisers review and may send an e-mail settlement offer through uFile (DCAD says online settlement is unavailable if you are represented by a tax consultant, already have a protest on file, or protest on a reason other than value; if you decline the offer no further offers are made under uFile). DCAD otherwise reaches out by phone or e-mail before the ARB hearing if the evidence warrants a change; if not contacted at least 3 days before the ARB hearing, call the division line. DCAD prefers phone/uFile over visiting the office, but the Customer Service lobby is open 7:30 AM-5:00 PM Mon-Fri.
